sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded (secrets.load(), R1) at process start, before the HTTP server accepts traffic. /healthz returns 200 only once the server is up, so ready means all three keys are already held.
sonnet.q2: The pod fails the load (retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, 4 attempts total), then exits non-zero and never becomes ready. The rollout halts and the old pods keep serving, so customers are unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background thread calls refresh() every 5 minutes and fetches the latest version of each secret. If the version id changed, it swaps in the new (value, version_id) pair in one step and logs the old and new version ids. If the read fails, errors or returns an empty value, the app keeps the last good value and logs a warning (secret name, error, held version id, never the value). It retries at the next interval and does not exit.
sonnet.q4: Values are held only in an in-memory map in the process (name -> (value, version_id)), read under a lock. They must never be logged, written to disk or placed in environment variables.
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod service identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*). Write: security on-call. Engineers have no access to prod values.
sonnet.q6: The old key values stay in git history, which is not rewritten, and in old images and old checkouts. They are treated as leaked. They are made harmless by rotating all three keys at the providers and then revoking the old ones.
sonnet.q7: Provider clients (PaymentsClient, EmailClient, GeocodingClient) do not store the key. They call secrets.get(name) on every request, which reads the in-memory map under a lock with no network call. An in-flight request keeps its old key and the next request uses the current one.
sonnet.q8: After at least 5 minutes plus a margin (e.g. 10 minutes) since the write, the team checks /healthz on each running pod directly (e.g. port-forward, not via the load balancer). Every pod must report the new version id, no pod may have logged a refresh warning, and provider error rates must be normal. Pod versions are re-checked immediately before revoking.
sonnet.q9: 1. Set access policies. 2. Copy keys into the store. 3. Build the code change (switch the app to the store, and remove api_key from config/app.yaml in the same pull request). 4. Deploy it. 5. Verify. 6. Rotate at the providers (then confirm, then revoke old keys). Removing keys from the committed file is part of step 3, not a separate later step.
sonnet.q10: From the store under orders-api/dev/* (sandbox keys), because make run sets APP_ENV=dev. It uses the developer's own credentials.
sonnet.q11: Any failure counts as a failed load for the whole set. The instance retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart (4 attempts in total), then exits non-zero. A missing secret is not explicitly described, but it is presumably such a failure, since the pod cannot load all three keys.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Security has not decided whether or how often to rotate on a schedule, and the plan sets no cadence.
